subject: lavaan WARNING: Could not compute standard errors!

messages.author: 1ade312b2b5688ec
messages.subject: lavaan WARNING: Could not compute standard errors!
parts:
Dear all,

I'm using the userGWAS() function to run a GWAS on a latent factor. Everything looks fine except that the "warning" column in result shows ""lavaan WARNING: Could not compute standard errors! The information matrix could not be inverted. This may be a symptom that the model is not identified." 
Should it be a concern? Do you have any suggestions to avoid this warning?

Thanks!

Best,
Stephen

messages.author: ac421cf36d1a4c37
messages.subject: Re: lavaan WARNING: Could not compute standard errors!
parts:
Dear Stephen,
The first thing I'd suggest is ensure that your your model is identified by running it with user model without the SNP effect. If it converges and produces SEs, then at least that portion of your model is identified. Then you need think about whether you are overspecifying your SNP effects. For this, I would suggest that you count the number of compound regression paths originating from the SNP. For k GWAS phenotypes you can typically only have k or fewer SNP effects in your model. If you have more than k SNP effects, the SNP portion of your model is likely underidentified.
All the best,
Elliot
